stem: A grower changes from a tall container to a much shorter container while using the same medium and irrigation schedule. What should be re-evaluated first?
choices: Fertilizer concentration, because changes in container height primarily alter nutrient concentration rather than moisture distribution.
Root-zone moisture distribution and drainage behavior because container geometry can change the proportion of the profile held near saturation.
Canopy temperature, because shorter containers generally change root-zone behavior mainly through their effect on leaf temperature.
The irrigation schedule can remain unchanged if medium composition is the same, because geometry has little effect on the vertical water profile.
rationale: Container geometry can alter the vertical distribution of water and the proportion of media near saturation, so irrigation assumptions should be revalidated.
